title: SVG to component documentation
description: Learn to generate framework components from SVG files with SVGER-CLI.
content: SVGER-CLI converts admitted SVG files into source components for React, React Native, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid, Preact, Lit, and browser-native JavaScript. Release status: package 4.1.0 is planned and unpublished. This site documents source behavior; it is not a release notice or npm availability guarantee. Start with a workflow Install the CLI, select a target framework, build a directory, and compile the generated files in the consuming application. SVGER generates source; it does not install framework runtimes. npm install --save-dev svger-cli npx svger build ./icons ./src/components/icons --framework react --typescript Choose a framework React and JSX · React Native · Vue 3 Angular · Svelte · Solid Preact · Lit · Vanilla DOM Documentation categories Getting started Build your first set of components and verify the output. CLI reference Commands, options, exit behavior, and safe workflows. Configuration Config files, precedence, naming, optimization, and examples. Build integrations Vite, Webpack, Rollup, Babel, Next.js, and Jest. SVG security Admission rules, external references, and trust boundaries. Live local comparison Run real SVGER and SVGR transforms on 50, 100, or 170 files. What the benchmark does—and does not—claim GitHub Pages cannot measure the CPU and resident memory of local Node processes. The benchmark page connects only after you start its loopback companion; metrics come from fresh local Node child processes. Results are host-specific and may favor either implementation. No preselected winner or synthetic result is displayed. Support and limits Read the installation guide , compiler and optimization limits , and troubleshooting guide . Input security, framework syntax validation, semantic coverage, and pixel comparison are distinct checks.

title: Getting started with SVGER-CLI
description: A practical first build: install SVGER-CLI, choose a framework, generate components, and validate them in your application.
content: This walkthrough takes an SVG folder to framework component files. Run commands from the consumer application's root so paths and configuration are predictable. 1. Install the CLI npm install --save-dev svger-cli The package supports Node.js according to its declared engine range. Use a currently supported Node LTS for production; see installation and runtime guidance . 2. Organize source icons Place trusted .svg files in a dedicated folder such as ./assets/icons . Keep originals in version control. The build discovers immediate children by default; use --recursive for nested folders. 3. Generate one target npx svger build ./assets/icons ./src/components/icons --framework react --typescript Choose one of the supported output targets . The target framework and its compiler remain the consuming app's responsibility. 4. Compile and inspect generated files Run the app's own TypeScript/framework build and tests. Review accessibility labels, IDs and references, CSS assumptions, dimensions, and the generated diff. A successful conversion is not proof of browser-rendering equivalence. 5. Make the build repeatable Commit configuration and generated outputs only if that matches your project policy. Use --check in CI to detect stale generated artifacts, and --dry-run to preview without writing. npx svger build ./assets/icons ./src/components/icons --framework react --check --format json Continue to the command reference or configuration guide .

title: Install SVGER-CLI
description: Install the SVGER-CLI package, check Node.js compatibility, and understand optional dependencies and package contents.
content: SVGER-CLI is installed as a project tool. It emits component source but does not bundle React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or other framework runtimes into your application. Install from npm npm install --save-dev svger-cli npx svger --version npx svger --help Package publication is controlled independently from this documentation. Check the npm registry for the version currently available to your account. Runtime compatibility Use the Node.js release table and the package's support matrix when selecting a runtime. The declared compatibility floor and currently security-supported Node releases are different concepts. Optional visual validation Raster-based --validate is optional and needs compatible separately installed packages. Ordinary source generation does not require the rasterizer. See optional dependency requirements before enabling it in CI. Development checkout Repository-only tests, benchmark tools, and the SVG sample corpus are not runtime dependencies. The sample corpus is maintained for project testing and is intentionally excluded from the npm package.

title: Framework support overview
description: Compare SVGER-CLI output targets, file types, language modes, runtime requirements, and framework-specific setup.
content: SVGER-CLI generates source files for nine target families. Install framework runtimes separately, then compile and test generated files in the consumer application. Target Common output Key note Guide React JSX / TSX Compile with your app's React toolchain React guide React Native JSX / TSX Requires react-native-svg in the app React Native guide Vue .vue Composition API option available Vue guide Angular .component.ts TypeScript required Angular guide Svelte .svelte Legacy remains default Svelte guide Solid JSX / TSX Validate with the Solid compiler Solid guide Preact JSX / TSX Use Preact's JSX runtime Preact guide Lit .js / .ts Web component output Lit guide Vanilla DOM .js / .ts Requires browser DOM at runtime Vanilla guide TypeScript is selected by default where supported. Use --no-typescript for JavaScript. Unsupported combinations return diagnostics instead of silently selecting another framework. Framework compiler and runtime conformance depends on the support matrix and version; see runtime guidance and troubleshooting .

title: Generate React SVG components
description: Generate JSX or TSX React components from SVG files with SVGER-CLI, including accessibility and validation guidance.
content: React output is generated as JavaScript or TypeScript component source. Install React and its compiler in the consuming application; SVGER-CLI does not add them as runtime dependencies. TypeScript TSX npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework react --typescript JavaScript JSX npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework react --no-typescript Use components with standard React imports from generated files. Check the output against your JSX runtime, lint rules, accessibility requirements, and the React version in your application. Review viewBox , title/label behavior, IDs, gradients, and references for each icon set. Single icon npx svger generate ./icons/search.svg ./src/icons --framework react --typescript For shared build pipelines, see Vite, Webpack, Rollup, Babel, Next.js, and Jest integration examples . For all framework outputs see the framework overview .

title: Generate React Native SVG components
description: Create React Native component source from SVG files and learn the react-native-svg runtime requirement.
content: React Native output uses React Native SVG primitives. The consuming application must install and configure react-native-svg ; generated source alone does not provide that runtime. npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework react-native --typescript Use --no-typescript for JavaScript output when supported by the target configuration. Validate in the actual app Native renderers differ from browser SVG. Compile with the app's React Native toolchain and test representative icons on supported platforms. Check gradients, masks, clipping, text, external references, and unsupported SVG features rather than assuming browser support maps exactly to native output. Security and asset handling SVG input is admitted before generation. External references are restricted by default. Review the security guide and framework overview .

title: Generate Vue 3 SVG components
description: Generate Vue single-file components from SVG files using Options or Composition API output.
content: Vue output uses .vue single-file components. Select Composition API script setup or the default component style where offered. Composition API npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework vue --typescript --composition JavaScript output npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework vue --no-typescript --composition Compile generated files with the Vue compiler version and bundler used by your app. Check component naming, props, SVG accessibility semantics, styling assumptions, IDs, and resource references in the generated output. Build integration Use the Vite or Webpack integration guide for build-time imports. See configuration precedence for persistent framework defaults.

title: Generate Angular SVG components
description: Generate TypeScript Angular components from SVG files, including standalone component workflows.
content: Angular generation requires TypeScript; JavaScript output is not supported for this target. The CLI creates source components and does not replace Angular workspace configuration. npx svger build ./icons ./src/app/icons --framework angular --typescript --standalone Use --standalone when appropriate for the target application. Compile with the app's Angular CLI and verify generated imports and metadata in that workspace. Module-based applications Omit --standalone when the output is intended for a module-oriented setup, then register components according to that application's architecture. Validate selectors, naming collisions, and accessibility behavior. Support Supported major lines are maintained in the support matrix ; compatibility outside that matrix may work but is not release-gated.

title: Generate Svelte SVG components
description: Generate Svelte components from SVG files and understand the default legacy path and explicit experimental IR mode.
content: SVGER-CLI writes .svelte component files. The legacy generator remains the default; the source candidate also has an explicitly selected static IR-v1 path for supported cases. Default generation npx svger build ./icons ./src/lib/icons --framework svelte --typescript Use --no-typescript for JavaScript components. Compile output with the Svelte toolchain in the consuming project. Explicit IR-v1 opt-in There is no dedicated CLI switch. Set svelteCompiler: "ir-v1" in .svgconfig.json or call the public compiler API with that option. Unsupported static constructs are rejected rather than silently falling back. This is not a claim of full dynamic-Svelte, CSS-cascade, browser rendering, or accessibility equivalence. { "framework": "svelte", "typescript": false, "svelteCompiler": "ir-v1" } Read the compiler limits and live benchmark methodology before comparing modes.

title: Generate Solid SVG components
description: Generate Solid JSX or TSX component source from SVG files and validate it with your Solid toolchain.
content: Solid output is generated as JavaScript or TypeScript component source. Install Solid and its build tooling in the consuming app. npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework solid --typescript npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons-js --framework solid --no-typescript Build the generated source with the same Solid compiler and JSX settings as the application. Verify props, SVG attributes, references, and accessibility behavior with representative inputs. The --signals option is available on the build command for applicable generator behavior; consult svger build --help for the installed version. See configuration and commands .

title: Generate Preact SVG components
description: Create Preact JSX or TSX components from SVG icons using SVGER-CLI.
content: Preact components are emitted as JSX or TSX source. Keep Preact, JSX transform settings, and any compatibility layer configured in the application itself. npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework preact --typescript npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons-js --framework preact --no-typescript Compile and render representative output with the project's Preact toolchain. Do not infer React runtime compatibility from syntactic JSX similarity. See bundler integrations and the framework overview .

title: Generate Lit SVG web components
description: Generate Lit TypeScript or JavaScript web components from SVG source files.
content: Lit output creates web component source. The consuming project must provide Lit and a browser-compatible build environment. npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework lit --typescript npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons-js --framework lit --no-typescript Validate custom-element names, shadow DOM styling, attributes, accessibility semantics, and browser support in the application. Test generated components in the actual target browsers. See input safety and troubleshooting .

title: Generate vanilla JavaScript SVG components
description: Generate framework-free browser DOM factories from SVG files using SVGER-CLI.
content: Vanilla output uses standard browser DOM facilities instead of a component framework. Generated code still requires a browser DOM when executed. npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons --framework vanilla --typescript npx svger build ./icons ./src/icons-js --framework vanilla --no-typescript Review output in the browser environment where it will run. Server-side Node execution without a DOM is not implied. Keep event handling, IDs, external resource policy, and accessibility labels in view. For framework output options, visit frameworks .

title: SVGER-CLI command reference
description: Reference for SVGER-CLI build, generate, watch, optimize, config, plugins, lock, recover, migrate, and clean commands.
content: The binary names are svger and svger-cli . Use the installed version's help output as the authority for the command surface. svger --help svger build <src> <out> --framework react --typescript svger generate ./icons/search.svg ./src/icons --framework svelte svger watch ./icons ./src/icons Build options --framework selects react, react-native, vue, angular, svelte, solid, preact, lit, or vanilla. TypeScript is the default where supported; use --no-typescript for JavaScript. Vue supports --composition , Angular supports --standalone . Builds also accept optimization, validation, include/exclude globs, recursion, hidden-file and symlink policies, collision policy, concurrency, file-count limits, dry-run/check/diff modes, and report formats. Maintenance svger optimize ./icon.svg ./out/icon.svg --level balanced svger config --init svger plugins svger lock ./icons/logo.svg svger unlock ./icons/logo.svg svger recover ./src/icons --format json svger migrate config .svgconfig.json --dry-run svger clean ./src/icons clean removes generated files from the chosen directory. Check the path before running it. Plugins execute with the invoking user's process permissions; load only trusted code. Deprecated aliases may warn. Read the complete CLI reference source for exact flags and migration behavior.

title: SVGER-CLI configuration guide
description: Configure framework, TypeScript, naming, optimization, file discovery, and compiler behavior for repeatable SVG builds.
content: SVGER reads .svgconfig.json from the working directory. Command options and project config combine into effective settings; inspect origins with config --explain . npx svger config --init npx svger config --set framework=vue npx svger config --set typescript=false npx svger config --set outputConfig.naming=kebab npx svger config --explain framework --format json Example configuration { "framework": "react", "typescript": true, "optimizationLevel": "basic", "recursive": false, "outputConfig": { "naming": "pascal" } } Use options supported by the installed version. Keep environment-specific paths in command invocations rather than sharing private machine paths in committed configs. Reproducibility and discovery Hidden files are skipped and symlinks ignored by default. Set recursive/include/exclude rules deliberately; enforce sensible file-count and input-size limits. Default output-name collisions fail so you can resolve ambiguous names explicitly. See CLI options , optimization levels , and security policy .

title: SVGER-CLI programmatic API
description: Use the public createSVGCompiler API to build components, inspect resolved configuration, and consume structured reports.
content: The public package root exports createSVGCompiler . It creates a scoped compiler service with build() and config.explain() . import { createSVGCompiler } from 'svger-cli'; const compiler = await createSVGCompiler({ cwd: process.cwd() }); const report = await compiler.build({ src: './icons', out: './src/generated/icons', framework: 'react', typescript: true, }); console.log(report.status, report.artifacts.length); Request fields include source/output paths, framework, language, optimization, selection, concurrency and safety policy. Validate reports and handle failure status in the calling application. Internal compiler modules are not public imports; rely on declarations from the installed package. Configuration explanation const entries = compiler.config.explain({ framework: 'svelte' }); For method signatures, inspect the installed dist/index.d.ts . Browse the generated API reference if present in the deployment, or the repository's TypeDoc output.

title: Bundler and test integrations
description: Configure SVGER-CLI with Vite, Webpack, Rollup, Babel, Next.js, and Jest using package subpath imports.
content: Use documented integration subpaths instead of running the CLI from a build hook. Integrations execute in the toolchain process; configure file scope and only load trusted plugins. Vite import { svgerVitePlugin } from 'svger-cli/vite'; export default { plugins: [svgerVitePlugin({ source: './src/icons', framework: 'react' })] }; Webpack const { SvgerWebpackPlugin } = require('svger-cli/webpack'); module.exports = { plugins: [new SvgerWebpackPlugin({ source: './src/icons', output: './src/generated' })] }; Other integrations Package subpaths are svger-cli/rollup , svger-cli/babel , svger-cli/nextjs , and svger-cli/jest . Confirm options and compatibility against the installed version and the full integration guide . Integrations are release-gated against the documented toolchain matrix; using a different major may work without being covered. Build plugins can write generated files or transform SVG imports depending on integration mode. Review source and destination paths, watch/HMR behavior, and CI permissions before enabling writes.

title: SVGER-CLI plugin guide
description: Develop and use SVGER-CLI plugins safely, with hook examples, lifecycle guidance, and trust-boundary notes.
content: Plugins extend processing hooks and run in the same process as SVGER-CLI. A plugin is executable code with the permissions of the invoking user—there is no plugin sandbox. Load a plugin svger plugins svger plugins --load ./plugins/my-plugin.js svger build ./icons ./out --plugin optimize,minify Only install or load plugins from sources you trust. Pin versions and review transitive packages; do not treat a plugin name or TypeScript type as a security boundary. Development Implement declared hooks, validate plugin metadata, avoid ambient network/filesystem access unless necessary, and return bounded diagnostics. Test hook ordering, errors, cleanup and repeated builds. See the plugin development guide for types and lifecycle contracts. Operational boundary Plugins receive no separate OS identity and are not isolated from the CLI. For high-risk untrusted plugin code, do not load it in a process containing credentials or sensitive paths.

title: SVG compiler and optimization limits
description: Understand SVGER-CLI optimization levels, Svelte IR opt-in status, semantic limits, and framework validation requirements.
content: Optimization rewrites SVG source; generation converts admitted input into framework syntax. Neither operation proves full browser behavior or pixel equivalence. Optimization levels Choose none , basic , balanced , aggressive , or maximum according to your tolerance for source changes. Preserve originals and validate output with your target renderer and application tests. Svelte IR-v1 The experimental static IR emitter is an explicit opt-in for Svelte only. Legacy remains default. Other framework IR emitters remain experiments and are not production routes. Unsupported IR syntax fails closed; it does not silently fall back. Coverage boundaries Static SVG conversion is not a browser, CSS cascade engine, external-resource resolver, or universal semantic analyzer. Text, references, CSS, filters, masks, foreign content and accessibility can have nuanced behavior. Review the security policy and run target framework compilation. Benchmark interpretation Use live local benchmarks to compare actual transforms on your machine. This site does not promise SVGER is faster: it reports measured wall time, CPU time, sampled RSS, output bytes, and successes for both implementations.

title: Migration and compatibility guide
description: Migrate earlier SVGER-CLI configuration and command usage while preserving reproducible output and release compatibility.
content: Before migrating, commit existing configuration and generated output, then run a preview. This project maintains a compatibility baseline; do not assume planned changes are published. svger migrate config .svgconfig.json --dry-run svger migrate config .svgconfig.json Migration targets include configuration, plugin declarations, and import forms. Backups are created by default for supported migrations. Review the report before accepting changes. Deprecated options V4 aliases such as --src , --out , and older naming flags may emit deprecation warnings. Prefer positional source/output arguments and configuration keys documented by the installed version. Version differences The documentation source may describe an unpublished candidate. Check svger --version , the package changelog, and the compatibility matrix before relying on new flags. See the migration guide .

title: SVG input security and safe use
description: Understand SVG admission, unsafe constructs, filesystem behavior, plugin trust, and limitations of SVGER-CLI security controls.
content: SVG files are untrusted structured input. SVGER-CLI validates inputs before generation and rejects selected unsafe constructs by default. This is defense in depth, not a guarantee that arbitrary generated code is harmless. Default rejection Active content, event handlers, unsafe URI forms, malformed XML, external references, and resource-limit violations are handled by the input safety policy. Exact rules are version-specific. Keep dependencies patched and review the security design record . Strip mode is not a sanitizer --unsafe-input-policy strip explicitly removes selected constructs and warns. Stripping can change meaning and does not establish semantic safety. Reject mode is preferred for ordinary workflows. Paths, outputs, and plugins Use isolated output directories, preserve backups, and review destructive commands such as clean . Build-tool plugins and extension code run with the host process permissions. Never load untrusted code in a process with secrets. Report security issues Follow the project's security reporting policy . Do not paste credentials or sensitive exploit material into public issues.

title: SVGER-CLI troubleshooting
description: Resolve common SVGER-CLI install, framework, SVG admission, path, collision, and benchmark setup issues.
content: CLI not found Install the package in the project, then use npx svger --help or the local package manager's executable path. Check that Node.js and npm are available. Unsupported framework option Use one of the accepted framework identifiers listed on the framework page . For exact behavior, consult the installed CLI's help output. Unsafe SVG rejected Review the diagnostic and source. Prefer correcting/removing unsafe external references or active markup. Strip mode is an explicit lossy policy, not a general sanitizer. Output collision Two input names may map to the same output component name. Rename source files or select a documented collision policy deliberately; default behavior fails rather than silently overwriting. Generated component fails framework compilation Verify the framework version, TS/JS mode, framework-specific dependencies, and integration options. Compile in the target application and share a minimal sanitized fixture when requesting help. Live benchmark cannot connect Start the local companion after building the repository and installing its benchmark-only dependencies. Keep it on the loopback address and allow the documented Pages origin. No hosted server is provided by GitHub Pages.

title: Live SVGER vs SVGR benchmark
description: Run real local SVGER-CLI and SVGR transforms on the same SVG corpus and compare time, CPU, sampled RSS, output size, and success counts.
content: Select 50, 100, or 170 source SVGs and compare the real local SVGER-CLI processor with SVGR's core JSX transform. The test runs only after you start a local companion and press Run. Local execution: GitHub Pages cannot execute Node packages or measure your process CPU/RAM. You must run the companion from a trusted clone. It binds to 127.0.0.1 ; this page sends only the selected count, and result data stays in your browser. SVG file count 50 files 100 files 170 files Run real comparison Not connected. Start the local companion using the instructions below. Download this run's JSON Start the companion npm run build npm --prefix tools/site-benchmark ci --ignore-scripts npm run benchmark:site For local preview, serve docs-site at http://localhost:8000 ; the companion permits that exact origin and the official project Pages origin. Check readiness from this page with the Run button; direct requests without an approved Origin are intentionally rejected. What the report measures Each engine runs in a fresh child process and receives the same deterministically sorted SVG inputs. The report includes wall time and Node process user/system CPU time for the transform loop, plus core-equivalent utilization (process CPU time divided by wall time; it is not whole-system CPU utilization), sampled peak resident set size (RSS), output bytes, output SHA-256, success/failure count, Node/package versions, and a fixture digest. Input loading, package import/startup and filesystem writes are excluded from timing; RSS includes the imported runtime and package baseline. RSS is sampled every 10ms and may miss short peaks, so it is not exact peak memory consumption. Fair interpretation Both engines generate React JavaScript in memory with a documented configuration. Different products can have different semantics, optimization defaults, error handling and generated output; this workload is not a security-equivalence test. If either implementation fails any input, the report shows counts and withholds a wall-time winner. Otherwise it reports the lower measured wall time for this run only. Do not treat results as a universal ranking or guaranteed advantage. Alternative implementation This comparison uses SVGR's @svgr/core and JSX plugin, version-pinned in the benchmark-only tool. Installing them does not modify SVGER-CLI's runtime dependencies or published package.
